question: Fixed mapping, requested clocks and work; does thermal state add net value to launch-offset selection? Actual-clock-invariant and throttle-mediated arms are separate.

workload.description: Two independent fixed-input FP16 GoogLeNet layer-group 0-9 work packets; A fixed to GPU, B fixed to DLA; 1000 repeats each. Not two full-network inferences.
workload.source: HaX-CoNN Table 2, author PDF page 4; timings are source anchors, not a recreated engine/runtime

uncertainty.method: 64 seeded Latin-hypercube points; engineering sensitivity set, not confidence region or certified joint hardware range

ablations: nominal 2x2x2 factorial: temperature-dependent leakage, contention and throttle. Periodic carry-over versus reset separately.

periodic.robust_subset: first 16 valid uncertainty IDs, at period 1.5 s

decision_rules.reversal: Two actions feasible in both states, opposite energy differences larger than 0.1% of each state's smaller energy and at least ten times observed numerical error; count best-action changes separately.
decision_rules.practical_value: Held-out state gain beyond best fixed policy; threshold residual, overhead break-even, feasibility, periodic persistence and parameter provenance all reported. No p-values on deterministic parameter rows.
decision_rules.success_is_not: Any single tuned reversal, or contention-only gains, or an oracle selected and evaluated on the same states.
